headline: A navigation redesign and a shared table system reshape the app as the depeg resolver starts locking forecasts.
fieldNotes: A heads-down week. The visible change is a navigation rework: a sticky core rail, a watch-column sidebar, and a homepage that rotates through what's worth looking at. Every table then moved onto one shared system, and a compare hub launched. Underneath, the resolver learned to withhold forecasts until it's actually ready, apxUSD's wobble got handled live, and a long correctness pass taught the data pipeline to fail closed rather than guess.

summary.label: Navigation & homepage redesign
summary.description: The sidebar becomes a lit 'watch column', a sticky core tape rail spans the top routes, and the homepage swaps static callouts for a rotating discovery module. The depeg resolver is promoted in primary navigation.

summary.label: Public compare hub
summary.description: A new indexable compare hub launches for side-by-side stablecoin lookups, the DEWS radar now surfaces high-risk coin logos scaled by escalation tier, and the public dataset catalog gains JSON-LD structured data.

summary.label: Resolver readiness & apxUSD
summary.description: The depeg resolver now locks predictions by forecast readiness or backstop behind a readiness contract, and /depeg gains a resolver posture board. The apxUSD incident reopened across DDR/DDRR with hardened pricing.

summary.label: Shared table system
summary.description: Content, status, analytics, comparison, and embedded detail tables migrate onto one shared table foundation with common toolbar controls, skeletons, density breakpoints, and accessible names.

summary.label: Reserves & yield
summary.description: Royco Dawn rows feed a new structured tranche-yield safety model, GBP, JPY, and AUD benchmarks move to direct central-bank sources (v8.22), and live-reserve coverage gains audit hardening and source fixes.

summary.label: Scoring & compliance
summary.description: Safety Score advances to v7.291, PegScore coverage extends to more priced assets, and a broad MiCA and GENIUS data pass refreshes compliance metadata across the registry.

summary.label: Pipeline fail-closed hardening
summary.description: Pricing, depeg, DEWS, yield, reserves, and blacklist paths now fail closed on stale or uncorroborated data, with freshness guards, input gating, and hardened parsing. The ops proxy now requires Access JWTs.

summary.label: Codebase consolidation
summary.description: A broad refactor wave shares helpers across worker, Telegram, and UI layers, derives types from schemas, and prunes dead code; perf work defers heavy detail bundles, memoizes the coverage matrix, and chunks cron queries.
